_readme: only see changes WITHIN an Act, so cross-Act succession is structurally invisible
to it — every one of the validation misses was this case. This file supplies it.
Scope note, deliberately narrow: act-level succession is recorded here because it
is unambiguous and public. Section-level concordance (IPC s.302 -> BNS s.103 and
so on) is NOT invented here. An incorrect section mapping in a litigation tool is
worse than an absent one, because it produces a confident, wrong citation. Fill
`sections` only from an authoritative concordance, and set verified=true per row
as a lawyer signs it off.
Act-level entries alone are already useful: they let the engine flag any pre-
commencement authority resting on a repealed Act as amber ('decided under the
repealed X; Y governs this matter'), which is correct without knowing the exact

successions.note: IPC repealed and replaced. Offences committed before commencement continue under the IPC; the repeal does not apply retrospectively to conduct already complete.

CrPC repealed and replaced. Procedural succession: pending proceedings are governed by savings provisions, so a procedural authority predating commencement needs checking against the saving clause rather than assuming it survives.

Evidence Act repealed and replaced. Evidence led on or after commencement is governed by the BSA, which is why applies_when is trial-based rather than cause-based. Section-level rows for this Act already exist, hand-verified, in data/mappings.json (M14-M17).
